title: Correction: The Minimal Phenomenal Experience questionnaire (MPE-92M): Towards a phenomenological profile of 'pure awareness' experiences in meditators

cost.compute_notes: One Crossref query, one Crossref updates-filter query, one PLOS JATS fetch. The notice is 4,362 bytes and was read in full.

claims.statement: The Data Availability statement of Gamma & Metzinger (2021) is incorrect; the correct URL for the MPE-92M data, documentation and all five language versions of the questionnaire is https://osf.io/xerhg/download.
claims.scope: The correction amends the Data Availability statement only. No result, table, figure or number in the 2021 article is amended.

our_assessment.why: Read in full from the PLOS JATS manuscript. Verified against the archive: api.osf.io/v2/guids/xerhg/ returns HTTP 200 with size 1301939, the zip was re-downloaded on 2026-09-08 and matches the archive's published sha256 exactly, and api.osf.io/v2/guids/gb76x/ returns HTTP 410 Gone. Both halves of the correction are true.

checked.how: urllib GET of the PLOS JATS manuscript; also api.crossref.org/works/10.1371/journal.pone.0314290 and the reciprocal api.crossref.org/works?filter=updates:10.1371/journal.pone.0253694
checked.result: Retrieved, 4,362 bytes. The updates filter on the 2021 DOI returns exactly one result, this notice; the reciprocal query on this DOI returns zero, which is the expected asymmetry and was checked so a zero could not be mistaken for a failed request. Copy kept at dev-science-ops/paper-retrospective-reproducibility/retrofit/papers/gamma2021-mpe92m/probe/correction_0314290.xml.

relations.why: Corrects the Data Availability statement only. The dead URL printed in the 2021 article (osf.io/gb76x) was formally replaced here on 2024-11-18, twenty-two months before this house re-checked it on 2026-08-25 and recorded it as a live problem. That is why this record exists: a corrected paper whose correction nobody looked for is a paper this house will report a defect against.
relations.asymmetric_note: The reciprocal edge cannot be WRITTEN: the vocabulary carries cito:corrects but no cito:isCorrectedBy, so gamma2021-mpe92m's own file says nothing about having been corrected. It is however DISCOVERABLE: `python tools/kb.py relations --of gamma2021-mpe92m` walks edges in both directions and prints this one. Checked 2026-09-08, after nearly recording the stronger and false claim that the fact was invisible. So the gap is in the FILE, not in the corpus -- which matters, because anyone reading paper.json directly, or any consumer that does not use kb.py, still sees an uncorrected paper.

open_questions: ANSWERED 2026-09-08, same session: the check was run over all 29 records carrying a DOI. TWO have formal corrections -- breznau2022-hidden-universe (10.1073/pnas.2410677121, Fig. 1 corrected, 2024-06-20) and gamma2021-mpe92m (this one). Base rate 2/29 = 6.9%. Raw output in corpus_corrections_audit.json. IMPORTANT AND UNCOMFORTABLE: the Breznau correction had ALREADY been found, on 2026-08-12, and recorded accurately. So the method does not never-check; it checks when the reader happens to notice, which on this evidence is one time in two.

The Breznau correction is recorded as artifact a6 with role `supplement`. A correction is not a supplement. That was the only slot available, and the consequence is that kb.py cannot answer `which papers in this corpus have been corrected?` -- the fact is reachable only by reading prose. Proposal for the standards repo: paper.schema.json should carry a first-class `updates` array (doi, type in {correction, retraction, expression-of-concern, addendum}, date, what_changed, affects_our_claims). record_status should gain nothing: a corrected paper is still active, and conflating correction with retraction is exactly what makes people avoid recording either.

13 of the 42 records carry no DOI at all -- 9 are our own reanalyses, 4 are arXiv/openreview-only. For those the Crossref updates filter cannot be run, and arXiv withdrawal and OpenReview status are different mechanisms with different endpoints. Nobody has checked those 4.
